summary: Drilldown latency percentiles on dashboard show stale per-route values after prefix-cache TTL rollover in eu-west
description:
Issue summary:
When a large prefix-cache TTL rollover completed in eu-west this morning, several LuminaHealth dashboard drilldowns that show per-route latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) continued to display the pre-rollover (stale) values for up to ~45 minutes. The aggregated dashboard tiles updated but drilldown queries remained anchored to the old prefix-cache shard until a manual cache invalidation.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: LuminaHealth reported alert noise and missed escalation because the drilldown didn't reflect the post-rollover latency regression for a small set of routes.
- Scope: Affects console drilldowns that rely on route-scoped percentile rollups where prefix-cache keys were rotated during TTL rollover. Observed in prod:eu-west only.

Environment:
- Prod (eu-west)
- Customer: LuminaHealth (enterprise) using pinned routes and per-route alerting
- Console version: 2026.02.8
- Ingest pipeline: kafka->ingest-service v3.4.1

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Triggered scheduled prefix-cache TTL rollover (automated job) at ~2026-03-10T05:00:00Z.
2) Dashboard summary tiles (route-level aggregates) reconciled within ~3 minutes.
3) Open route drilldown (clicking tile to see per-request percentile chart) still returned the previous shard's rollup values for multiple routes.
4) Manual cache invalidation for the affected shard (console /admin/cache/invalidate) caused drilldowns to return fresh values within ~30–60s.

Logs/observations:
- Ingest service logs show rollup writes to new prefix keys at 05:01:12Z.
- Console query traces show successful reads but with cache-key pointing to old shard until manual invalidation.
- No 5xx errors; query latency was normal.
- Alerting engine evaluated rule on summary tiles and fired correctly; the drilldown-linked evaluation was stale and did not trigger escalation.

Expected behaviour:
- After prefix-cache TTL rollover, both summary tiles and drilldown queries should observe new rollup keys consistently within the rollout window (we expect <5 minutes for full reconciliation).

Workaround currently in use:
- Manual cache invalidation for the affected prefix shard via internal admin tool.

Customer impact notes:
- LuminaHealth recorded a delayed incident response costing ~20 minutes. They requested a post-incident note and recommendation to avoid recurrence.

investigation_notes: Query traces: console->rollup-reader shows cache key resolution logic preferred local shard mapping when rotation marker absent.

Hypothesis: rotation job rotates prefix keys, writes new rollup outputs, but rotation marker (small metadata write) sometimes lagged behind due to transient ZK (coordination) latency; readers continued to resolve to previous mapping for some time.
Reproducible in staging by artificially injecting 50–200ms latency into coordination service; reproduced with 25% probability when marker write delayed >30s.

Metrics: increased 'coordination.write.latency' around 05:00Z; DLQ counts unchanged. No consumer lag spikes on kafka.
Dashboards show ~0.2s spike in writer latency and 35s tail in rotation marker ack.
Temporary mitigation validated: on cache-miss, reader can query rollup-metadata endpoint for explicit fallback; implementing this as short-term fix to avoid manual invalidation requirement.
Related configs: prefix-cache TTL configured to 3600s and automated rotation randomized across shards; under high cardinality bursts rotation markers fell behind occasionally.
Related linked tickets: SUP-472396 (dashboard-heatmap-hour-shift-after-reindex) - background: previous reindexing introduced schema migration touching rollup metadata handling.
Risk assessment: medium — affects drilldowns and alerting escalation; can be triggered during maintenance/rotation windows but not under steady-state traffic.
resolution_notes:
Hotfix scheduled: (1) Guard rotation completion until rotation-marker ack confirmed by at least 2 console-readers (deployed 2026-03-14 to eu-west), (2) Add temporary fallback in read-path to consult rollup-metadata on cache-miss before returning stale values (deployed 2026-03-13 as emergency patch), (3) Instrumentation dashboard created for coordination.write.latency and rotation-marker-ack tails.

Workaround for customers: run admin cache invalidation for affected prefix shard if drilldown shows mismatch with summary tiles.

Follow-ups: (A) Post-deployment runbook update to include detection (summary vs drilldown divergence), (B) Backfill low-risk shards with rotation-marker reconciliation job over the next 48 hours, (C) Schedule a postmortem with LuminaHealth ops and platform eng (invite list created).

Customer notification: LuminaHealth informed 2026-03-13 12:00Z with apology, summary of root cause, and planned remediation timeline. Ticket will be closed after eu-west hotfix verification and customer sign-off.
